newsitem.title: USA: Capstone acquires Beverly pharmacy unit for $825 million.
newsitem.headline: Capstone acquires Beverly pharmacy unit for $825 million.

text.p: Capstone Pharmacy Services Inc. has agreed to acquire Beverly Enterprises Inc.'s Pharmacy Corporation of America unit in a deal worth $825 million, the companies said Wednesday.

The deal would create the largest independent U.S. institutional pharmacy company, with revenues of about $900 million, some 30 percent higher than its nearest competitor, the companies said. It will serve the pharmaceutical and medical needs of nearly 500,000 customers and operate about 100 institutional pharmacies in 32 states.

Under the definitive agreement, Capstone will issue about 50 million shares of its stock to Beverly shareholders and assume $275 million of debt. Capstone will offer about 0.44 of a share of its stock for each Beverly share on a fully diluted basis.
Capstone's stock fell $1.81 to $9.94 on Nasdaq. Beverly rose 12.5 cents to $14.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Beverly shareholders cumulatively will own about 57 percent of the combined pharmacy company, but Beverly will not retain any ownership position in the merged company.
The remainder of Beverly's business -- excluding its Pharmacy Corporation of America unit -- will retain the company's name.

Shares of the "new Beverly" company -- comprised of skilled nursing centres, transitional care hospitals and rehabilitation therapy operations -- will be distributed to Beverly shareholders on the effective date of the deal on a one-for-one share basis. The new Beverly's shares will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

"There are significant synergies between PCA and Capstone that should enable the expanded company to improve customer service, reduce purchasing and operating costs and broaden the scope of its operations to take full advantage of market opportunities," said Beverly Chairman David Banks.
"We estimate the annual value of these potential synergies at about $25 million, which represents a significant financial advantage for the combined company."
The transaction will boost Capstone's annual earnings per share by at least 10 percent, the companies said.
Capstone, based in Baltimore, Md., is a leading provider of institutional pharmacy services to long-term care facilities and correctional institutions.

Beverly, based in Fort Smith, Ark., is a leading provider of post-acute health care. In addition to institutional and mail service pharmacies, Beverly operates 630 skilled nursing and rehabilitation centres, as well as outpatient therapy clinics, assisted living facilities, and hospice and home health agencies.
